newsitem.title: USA: Latin Brady bonds lower, focus on Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Latin Brady bonds lower, focus on Bulgaria.

text.p: Latin American Brady bonds were lower across the board in line with the U.S. Treasury market, but dealers said the broader focus was on Bulgaria following the victory by the Union of Democratic Forces (UDF).
"Bulgaria had a good rally waiting for the elections. So it's a situation now where it is 'buy on rumor sell on the fact,'" said one trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
The UDF won an absolute majority in parliament in Saturday's elections with 52 percent of the votes.

Market experts said a UDF victory was pretty much anticipated and that was reflected in the price gains of Bulgarian debt instruments in the run-up to the elections. But now some market experts believe Bulgarian Bradys may be rangebound until there is progress on reforms and until there the program agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is implemented.

"Obviously, in spite of this good news, Bulgaria is heavily indebted and will have a very difficult implementation period," said Kurt Schmid, managing director of emerging markets trading at SBC Warburg in New York.

"They (Bulgaria) will get a lot of help and I think default is not very likely anymore, but the country risk remains relativly high and I think at current values, at least relative to other countries, it is probably correctly valued," Schmid said.
Bulgarian IABs reversed 1/4 point gains scored in London earlier today, falling 5/8 to 60-1/4 bid. The country's FLRBs also retraced 1/4 point gains slipping 3/4 to 44-3/4 bid.
Longer term though, market experts said Bulgarian yield spreads could narrow.

"If and when the positive effects of the reforms start kicking in, I think spreads will tighten, but I think at these levels the market really wants to see what is happening and it will now be a much more gradual" type of price movement," said another source.
In the broader market, prices moved in tandem with U.S. Treasuries in what traders called a dull market.

"It's the same story. We are tightening or widening five to 10 basis points with the U.S. Treasury market. We are just dancing around these levels," said the first trader, who expects it to be a very quiet week for the Brady bond market.
At 1600 EDT/2100 GMT, Argentine FRBs were 1/8 softer at 89-5/8 bid, Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/4 lower at 74-1/4 bid and Mexican pars were 3/8 weaker at 70-3/8 bid.
